sources.role: Public entry page for the combined charter boat and fishing guide permit lookup
sources.scope: Statewide. The page says charter boats and fishing guides are permitted by the Commission and offers three static HTML sorts: county of business, business name, and guide name. It does not filter by water, port, or hull.
sources.credential_holder: The person who holds the annual Charter Boat/Fishing Guide permit. The statute and the regulations use one permit for both a charter boat operator and a fishing guide.
sources.access: Public HTML. No login. The page links the three roster files, the application service, the how-to PDF, and 58 Pa. Code Chapter 51, Subchapter L.
sources.rights_basis: The page publishes a lookup and states no commercial-reuse, redistribution, attribution, or bulk-access license. Its roster footer links to a short PFBC policy index, which links to the Commonwealth privacy policy. That policy covers visitor information. It does not license site content.
sources.bulk: No API and no open-data file on this page. The lookup is three HTML files.
sources.request_process: Program questions go to the agency mailbox printed on the page. That invitation is not a reuse grant. A separate Right-to-Know process is published for Commission records.

sources.role: Business-sorted roster of permitted charter boats and fishing guides
sources.scope: Statewide combined permit holders. Parsed on the checked date as 579 business rows and 658 guide-name slots. 35 businesses list more than one guide name. One business lists 18. County of business is an address county. Erie County is 74 business rows and 78 guide-name slots. The file also has business-address counties New York 29, Ohio 8, New Jersey 10, Maryland 7, West Virginia 2, and Other 12. No water, port, vessel, permit-type, or permit-number column.
sources.credential_holder: Each guide name is printed as the permit holder associated with a business. The file does not say whether that person is acting as a charter boat operator or as a fishing guide.
sources.access: Public static HTML. Last-Modified header Wed, 25 Nov 2026 02:05:02 GMT. Columns are Business Name and Address, County of Business, and Guide Name and Cell Phone. A Business Website control is present on 303 of 579 rows. Of those controls, 255 values look like URLs, 18 look like street addresses, 6 are email addresses, 15 are blank claims such as n/a or none, and 9 are other text. There is no query filter.
sources.rights_basis: The file footer links to webprivacy.htm and does not state a copyright license, a public-domain dedication, or permission to copy the roster into a commercial directory. webprivacy.htm only links the Commonwealth accessibility, privacy, and security policies.
sources.bulk: One HTML file. No documented bulk feed. Report1.htm, sorted by county, parsed to the same 579 data rows. The agency does not print a total on the page.
sources.request_process: No roster-specific permission form. Use the permit-program contact on the landing page or the Commission's Right-to-Know process. Neither is a standing commercial license.

sources.scope: How a person buys the combined permit. Not a public fleet search. States the permit is required on Commonwealth waters including boundary waters. Posted prices are $101.97 resident and $401.97 nonresident, described as including a $1.00 issuing-agent fee and a $0.97 transaction fee. The statute fee schedule checked the same day lists $100 resident and $400 nonresident before those add-ons.
sources.credential_holder: Applicant for the Charter Boat/Fishing Guide permit. Online catalog codes printed in the how-to PDF are 178 for a resident and 179 for a nonresident.
sources.access: Public page. Application itself is an account purchase at HuntFish.PA.gov. The how-to PDF at https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/fishandboat/documents/about-us/affiliates/charters-guides/charterboatfishingguide-howtoguide.pdf describes cart steps and a printable permit. It is not a field dictionary for the public roster.
sources.rights_basis: Application instructions do not grant reuse of the public roster or of issued permits.
sources.request_process: Online purchase through HuntFish.PA.gov. Questions use the permit mailbox on the page.

sources.publisher: Pennsylvania Code and Bulletin, publishing 58 Pa. Code Chapter 51, Subchapter L
sources.role: Binding definitions and operating rules for the permit
sources.scope: Defines charter boat as a boat operated as a commercial enterprise that carries passengers for hire to fish on Commonwealth waters. Defines charter boat operator as the person in actual physical control of that boat. Defines fishing guide as a person who guides or leads others to fish, for any consideration. One permit covers both activities, is valid for the calendar year, and expires December 31. Advertising guide or charter services is prima facie evidence of a commercial enterprise. A boat launch in Pennsylvania creates a rebuttable presumption of operating on Commonwealth boundary waters. When a boat is used, the operator needs a Commission or NASBLA boating-safety certificate or a U.S. Coast Guard boat-operator license. Insurance minimum, amended effective August 30, 2025, is $250,000 each occurrence and $500,000 aggregate. The code site says it reflects changes effective through 56 Pa.B. 6006 (September 5, 2026).
sources.credential_holder: Charter boat operator or fishing guide. The credential is the person, not the hull. The regulations do not require the public roster to name a vessel.
sources.access: Public HTML of the Pennsylvania Code.
sources.rights_basis: The code site states: No part of the information on this site may be reproduced for profit or sold for profit. It also says the HTML is drawn from the official full-text database and may differ slightly from the printed code.
sources.attribution: The site does not offer an attribution license. The profit bar is a limit, not a credit line.
sources.bulk: No bulk feed of permit holders. This source is regulatory text.
sources.request_process: None stated for commercial reproduction. Silence on a permission form is recorded as unknown beyond the posted profit bar.

sources.role: Statute creating the charter boat and fishing guide permit
sources.scope: 30 Pa.C.S. § 2907.3. Operating a charter boat or a fishing guide operation on Commonwealth waters without the permit is unlawful. Definitions match the regulation: a charter boat is the boat; a fishing guide is the person. Added by Act 159 of 2004, with a 2020 amendment to issuing-agent status. Fee cross-reference is section 2715, which on the checked official title states a $100 resident and $400 nonresident charter boat/fishing guide permit.
sources.access: Public official statute HTML. Title 30 PDF was also located at https://www.legis.state.pa.us/WU01/LI/LI/CT/PDF/30/30.PDF and shows the same section.
sources.rights_basis: The statute page states the legal duty to hold a permit. It does not grant or deny reuse of the Commission's published roster.

sources.role: Statutory limit on Commission records that contain personal information
sources.scope: 30 Pa.C.S. § 324. Records maintained by the Commission or its issuing agents that contain a home address or other personal information, including fishing licenses, boat registrations, and permits and applications, are not public records under the cited Right-to-Know Law. A note on the page says the 1957 citation was repealed and replaced by the 2008 Right-to-Know Law.
sources.rights_basis: The section withholds permit and application records that contain home addresses and personal information from the public-record definition. It does not convert the separately posted HTML roster into a licensed dataset. The posted roster still prints business addresses and cell phones. That posting was not read as permission to copy those details.
sources.bulk: Mailing lists of permit holders are not authorized by this section.
sources.request_process: Right-to-Know requests are a different access path and still do not, by themselves, license commercial republication.

sources.role: Published process for requesting Commission records
sources.scope: Restates 58 Pa. Code § 51.9. Public records are available for inspection and duplication on business days. Requests must be written. Anonymous and oral requests are not accepted. Fees follow the Office of Open Records, with certified copies at $1 per page up to $5 per document. The page cites 30 Pa.C.S. §§ 324 and 5503 alongside the Right-to-Know Law.
sources.access: Public HTML. Standard request forms are linked from the Office of Open Records.
sources.rights_basis: A Right-to-Know response is access to a public record. The page does not say that a granted request, or the already posted roster, may be republished in a commercial directory. Intended-use limits are not stated on this page.
sources.bulk: Copies are produced on request and may require prepayment above $100. This is not an open bulk feed.
sources.request_process: Written request to the Director, Bureau of Administration, by mail, fax, email, or in person, using the address and agency mailbox on the page. Appeals go to the Office of Open Records within 15 business days.

sources.role: Rule for release of boat-title facts
sources.scope: 58 Pa. Code § 93.117. For a specifically identified titled boat, the Commission will provide owner name, lienholder name and address, title date, and make, model, and year. It will not release a title holder's home address except by consent, court order, or subpoena. It will not release mailing lists or records of title holders except to government agencies for official purposes.
sources.credential_holder: Boat title holder, who may be a different person from the fishing-guide permit holder. The charter roster does not carry title fields.
sources.rights_basis: Same code-site bar on reproduction for profit. The section itself forbids release of title-holder mailing lists outside official government use. A one-boat written request is not a directory feed.
sources.bulk: Mailing lists and records of title holders are not released for this use.
sources.request_process: Written request that specifically identifies a particular boat. No published process for a fleet extract.

sources.publisher: Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, Office of Administration
sources.role: License for datasets that are actually published on data.pa.gov
sources.scope: Data sets on data.pa.gov are offered free and without restriction, as is, with attribution requested and not required. The policy does not create an enforceable right. A catalog search limited to data.pa.gov for charter boat, fishing guide, and Fish and Boat returned State Parks, PALS sales outlets, recreation locations, and Game Commission hunting agents. It did not return a charter boat or fishing guide roster. PALS_Sales_Outlets, viewed in the catalog, is license-sales locations, not permit holders.
sources.access: Public policy page. Catalog API checked at https://data.pa.gov/api/catalog/v1 with domains=data.pa.gov.
sources.rights_basis: The unrestricted grant applies only to data sets offered on data.pa.gov. The charter and guide roster is not one of those data sets, so this grant does not cover it.
sources.attribution: Requested, not required, for data retrieved from data.pa.gov.
sources.bulk: Portal datasets can be downloaded. The roster is not among them.
sources.request_process: No process on this page for asking an agency to add a dataset.

sources.role: Visitor privacy policy linked from the roster footer
sources.scope: Governs information the Commonwealth collects from people who visit its sites. It says the Commonwealth does not collect or use personal information for commercial marketing and will not sell or rent personal information collected online except as provided by law. That sentence is about the Commonwealth's own use of visitor data.
sources.access: Public HTML. The roster reaches it through https://pfbc.pa.gov/webprivacy.htm.
sources.rights_basis: No copyright license, public-domain dedication, or permission to reproduce agency directories. The external-link section says the Commonwealth cannot authorize use of copyrighted materials on external websites. Users must ask the external sponsor.

sources.role: Public landing and marina on Lake Erie
sources.scope: Walnut Creek Marina is owned by the Commonwealth and operated by the Commission on Lake Erie at Fairview. It has 72 seasonal slips, six concrete motorboat ramps, and one hand-carry ramp. The page says charter boats and fishing guides that operate out of the marina can be found at the statewide roster. That link is the unfiltered statewide list, not a Walnut Creek fleet.
sources.access: Public HTML. Slip waiting list is a separate application. The marina is a landing, not a credential authority.
sources.rights_basis: The marina page does not license reuse of tenant or charter names. It also does not publish a departure roster.
sources.request_process: Seasonal slip waiting-list application linked from the page. That is for mooring, not for directory permission.

sources.role: Membership captain directory for a Lake Erie charter association
sources.scope: Captain members, not the licensed population. The page checked on this date has 32 named captain entries plus a blank template row that was not counted. One entry names Dunkirk, New York, as the port. Two entries say multi-port. Twenty-nine name a Pennsylvania port. Two entries each name two captains on one vessel. Two entries are two captains on one shared vessel listing that is repeated. The directory names a port and a vessel. It is not a PFBC extract and it has no as-of date on the page. The association homepage news block was marked updated 11/14/26.
sources.credential_holder: Bylaws limit captain membership to a person licensed to operate a charter boat for hire on the Great Lakes or inland waters of the United States. That is a membership rule. It does not identify which license, and the directory does not print a PFBC permit number.
sources.access: Public HTML at epacba.com/captains.htm. Homepage https://epacba.com/ describes five paid membership classes and online renewal for 2027.
sources.rights_basis: June 2015 Rev3 bylaws say a captain member will be listed in the Captains Directory, and that unpaid members have online listings removed. The bylaws contain no copyright license, no commercial-reuse grant, and no bulk-download permission. No website terms page was found.
sources.bulk: No download or API. The directory is one HTML page.
sources.request_process: Membership application linked from the homepage. Joining is not a license for a third party to republish the directory.

highest_priority_permission_question: Does the Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission authorize a commercial directory to copy, redistribute, and keep current the posted Charter Boat/Fishing Guide roster? Public viewing, a Right-to-Know request, and a commercial-reuse license are different things. The HTML files and the privacy policy they link do not grant that license. 30 Pa.C.S. § 324 says Commission permit records that contain home addresses and personal information are not public records. The Pennsylvania Code site bars reproduction of the regulatory text for profit. The data.pa.gov unrestricted license does not apply because the roster is not published there.
recommended_first_source: Use https://pfbc.pa.gov/images/admin/guides/Report2.htm only as the current credential lookup, reached from https://www.pa.gov/agencies/fishandboat/about-us/affiliates/charter-boats-and-fishing-guides. Do not treat Erie County, a business name, or an association port as the Lake Erie fleet. Get written commercial-reuse terms from the Commission before copying the roster.
